description: Patients none of whose lab records has an RA result of '-'.

a.request: Among patients none of whose laboratory records has a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of '-', list the 10 with the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records. Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest hematocrit first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Averages ignore missing values. Don't round.
a.sql: SELECT p.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS average_ua, AVG(l.HCT) AS average_hematocrit FROM Patient AS p LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS r WHERE r.ID = p.ID AND r.RA = '-') GROUP BY p.ID ORDER BY average_hematocrit IS NULL, average_hematocrit DESC, p.ID LIMIT 10

d.request: Among patients with no laboratory record where `RA = '-'`, list the 10 patients with the highest average `HCT` across their laboratory records, showing patient `ID`, average `UA`, and average `HCT` in descending average `HCT` order, with patients lacking `HCT` values last; exclude null values from each average and do not round.
d.sql: SELECT p.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS average_UA, AVG(l.HCT) AS average_HCT FROM Patient AS p LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS r WHERE r.ID = p.ID AND r.RA = '-') GROUP BY p.ID ORDER BY average_HCT IS NULL, average_HCT DESC, p.ID LIMIT 10

c.request: Looking only at patients without a rheumatoid factor (`RA`) result of '-' in their lab tests, which 10 have the highest average hematocrit (`HCT`) across all their lab records? Show patient `ID`, average uric acid (`UA`) and average hematocrit, highest first, with patients who have no hematocrit values last. Ignore missing values in the averages and don't round. Patients none of whose lab records has an RA result of '-'.
c.sql: SELECT p.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS avg_ua, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_hct FROM Patient AS p LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS r WHERE r.ID = p.ID AND r.RA = '-') GROUP BY p.ID ORDER BY avg_hct IS NULL, avg_hct DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: Among patients with no laboratory record where `RA = '-'`, list the 10 with the highest average `HCT` across all their lab records, showing patient `ID`, average `UA`, and average `HCT`. Ignore NULL values in each average, do not round, and place patients with no `HCT` values last.
b.sql: SELECT p.ID, AVG(l.UA) AS avg_UA, AVG(l.HCT) AS avg_HCT FROM Patient AS p LEFT JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory AS r WHERE r.ID = p.ID AND r.RA = '-') GROUP BY p.ID ORDER BY AVG(l.HCT) IS NULL, AVG(l.HCT) DESC, p.ID LIMIT 10;
